title: Majestic Checks
transcript: You see black is up six points of material having two extra pawns and two rooks for two minor pieces. But as I've told you many times, the most important aspect in chess is piece activity. And although black is threatening a checkmate in one move, it is white to move and these white pieces are surrounding the black king. [music] So let us not resign and let's look for checks. We can easily exclude queen to h6 check. This is a free queen and no follow-up check leads to anything. And the same applies to queen to d4 or queen to e5 check. Those would be free queens for black. Queen to f6 check might seem promising, but after king to g8, we have no way of checkmating the king. And if we desperately try to sacrifice the knight to prepare a checkmate, black doesn't even have to take. This is just a checkmate. Bishop f6 seems promising because if the king takes, we actually have a checkmate in two moves. But unfortunately, the king can go to g8. And if you try to prepare a checkmate with queen to h6, black will have another checkmate in two moves. So is this position just winning for black? Well, not exactly. There is one more check that we didn't consider. Knight to e6 check. First of all, if the king moves back, now we still have queen to b8 check and checkmate. And if the pawn takes, we have queen f8 with a dovetail checkmate. But of course, the most resilient move for black is to take the knight with the queen, not allowing the queen to go to f8. But when you're calculating checks, you have to follow the new checks that you have created. And in this case, we have opened up the possibility for bishop to f8 check. So we have to consider it. But it's not hard to see that this doesn't lead anywhere. This queen check at best wins you back a rook, but you're still completely losing in one move. But looking at the new checks is not the only thing we have to do when considering a new position. No, we have to also re-evaluate those checks that we had discarded previously. So, let's do the same process. Queen to E5 check, free queen. Queen to F6 check, free bishop. What about queen to D4 check? After F6, there is no follow-up. If we give another check, we can chase the king around for a little bit, but eventually he's going to go to safety. So, the final check we have to look at is the brilliant and majestic queen to H6. Because of course, if the king goes back to either one of these squares, queen to F8 is just going to be a checkmate. But if the king takes, now we have placed his king in a very uncomfortable position. We only have two checks to consider. Obviously, bishop to G5 doesn't work, but what does work is bishop to F8. Checkmate.
